newsitem.title: NORWAY: Jittery Oslo bourse slides 2 pct, outlook nervous.
newsitem.headline: Jittery Oslo bourse slides 2 pct, outlook nervous.

text.p: Norwegian shares took a slide on Thursday on continuing jitters over the inflation outlook in the oil-rich country and because of nervousness over foreign, especially U.S., interest rates.
Dealers said the market was likely to remain cautious ahead of the meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve next Tuesday.
Oslo's Total share index tumbled 2.13 percent to end at 1,055.53 points in turnover of 1.82 billion crowns.
"It's been a tremendous year to now and sentiment is becoming bearish," said one broker.
"There's a lot of psychology in the market at the moment and people want to get out. There are too many risk factors."
Total turnover was boosted by 547 million crowns from the final transaction in the takeover of insurer Protector ASA by Swiss group Zurich Insurance Co.
Business also was hetic in the financial sector's Fokus Bank, which this week proposed a merger with Bolig og Naeringsbanken (BNbank).
Fokus closed 0.50 crowns up at 59.50 crowns in trade worth 203 million crowns, while BNbank gained 3.50 crowns to 193.50 crowns in turnover of nearly 70 million crowns.
